comment: Fan Control: FanControlUI's settings pane, editors, alerts and power profiles, and the glue in Sources/FanControlGlue/ (widgets, live activity). FanControlUI looks its labels up in the app's Localizable.strings.
keys: Installed manually, pinned to another build
The installed helper is pinned to a different build of DynamicNotch and refuses this app. Re-run sudo install.sh with this app (FanControl/Support/manual-install/), then click Check Again.
The installed helper’s code signature does not match what DynamicNotch expects. Re-run sudo install.sh with this app (FanControl/Support/manual-install/), then click Check Again.
Allow “DynamicNotch” in System Settings ▸ General ▸ Login Items & Extensions (macOS 15) / Login Items (macOS 14) to let it change fan speeds.
Reading temperatures works without the helper. Changing fan speeds requires installing it (administrator approval is needed).

Slow Down Polling on Battery (10 s)
Another fan control app (%@) is running. If both write at the same time they will override each other.
The alert and the all-fans-maximum override turn on when the hottest CPU/GPU sensor reaches these temperatures, and off again once it has cooled by the hysteresis.
macOS (the SMC) controls every fan, so there is no curve. Fan control returns the fans to automatic.
Every fan at a constant %@ RPM (limited to each fan's range): the curve is a flat line. Read-only preset.
Every fan at full speed (%@ RPM, limited to each fan's maximum): a flat line at the top of the chart. The loudest setting. Read-only preset.
Every fan follows %@ on a smooth curve through %@, reaching full speed well before the emergency threshold. Read-only preset.
Note: CPU (max) is the hottest core, which idles at about 72–78 °C on Apple Silicon, so Boost runs the fans at about 5,500 RPM or more even when the Mac is idle.
Editable profile. Choose a mode for each fan; a sensor-based fan follows its own curve (drag the points or use the rows below). Then Save or Apply.
Fix the fan curve before saving.
%@ is not available: the fan would run at maximum speed.
A curve needs at least two points.
Every point needs a temperature between 0 and 130 °C.
Two points have the same temperature.
A point is outside this fan's range (%@–%@ RPM).
The speed falls from %@ to %@ RPM between %@ and %@: the fan slows down as it gets hotter.
Full speed only at %@, at or above the emergency threshold (%@).
The curve never reaches this fan's maximum (%@ RPM). Only the emergency override (%@) runs it at full speed.
Turn on Fan Control in Settings to read temperatures.
The history is kept while DynamicNotch runs (about 30 minutes) and is not saved.
The dashed line is the high-temperature alert threshold (%@), set in Settings ▸ Fan Control ▸ General. CPU and GPU values turn orange within 10° below it and red at or above it.
CPU, GPU and SSD temperatures are shown by the Temperature widget.
Let the power profile rules choose the fan profile again

Rules are checked from top to bottom and the first one that matches decides. A fan profile you choose by hand stays until the situation changes. Low Power Mode is changed through the fan control helper and given back to your own setting when no rule asks for it.
No rules yet. Add one below, or start from a template.
Precedence: a profile you choose by hand, then emergency and workload rules, then power profiles, then your own profile. The all-fans-maximum safety override always applies.
Never used: an earlier rule matches everything.
Times wrap past midnight (22:00 to 07:00 is overnight). Same start and end means all day. No day selected means every day.
Needs the fan control helper (install.sh). Sets Low Power Mode for all power sources, like “Always” or “Never” in System Settings.
